reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BNB staking with a fixed daily return, directs viewers to external destinations, and invites them to join and make money immediately. The displayed Deposit control and BNB Harvest Daily ROI connect the offer to a solicitation to place BNB into the presented service. Audit-report and CertiK branding appear alongside the offer, but their authenticity, endorsement, and scope are not established, and one dashboard shows 3% instead of the separately advertised 5% return.

citations.quote: stake BNB and earn a fixed 5% everyday
Stake BNB & Earn 5% Daily ROI! Website: https://bnbharvest.com/ Telegram Chat: https://t.me/bnbharvest
the smart contract successfully passed its audit by Certick join us and start making money right now

opening.argument: Judge, the return claim deserves scrutiny, but the material does not present a consistent return figure. The narration says the return is fixed at 5% every day, while a displayed dashboard says 3% Daily ROI. That discrepancy limits what can be concluded about the terms actually available through the service. The audit claim also appears as the promoter's assertion, not as independently established protection for anyone who participates. The defensible reading is a questionable service promotion, not a demonstrated deception.

citations.quote: stake BNB and earn a fixed 5% everyday
the smart contract successfully passed its audit by Certick

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution correctly identifies a staking pitch and external destinations. But its own observation that the dashboard shows 3% rather than the advertised 5% cuts against treating the asserted rate as an established operating term. A displayed Deposit control shows an interface, not a completed deposit or payment outcome; the audit claim remains an assertion whose scope the video does not verify.

citations.quote: Stake BNB & Earn 5% Daily ROI! Website: https://bnbharvest.com/ Telegram Chat: https://t.me/bnbharvest

true_side_reply.rebuttal: No risk warning or qualification accompanies the pitch. An inconsistent dashboard rate does not make the solicitation cautious: the video still tells viewers to stake BNB for a fixed daily return and urges them to join immediately. The absence of a completed deposit does not change what the promotion asks viewers to do.

citations.quote: stake BNB and earn a fixed 5% everyday
join us and start making money right now

opening.argument: Judge, the video spends part of its presentation showing what the service's dashboard looks like: a Daily ROI panel, deposit and harvest controls, and an audit-report graphic. Those views can help a viewer inspect the proposed service without establishing that the displayed figures are verified earnings or that anyone completed a transaction. The competing 3% dashboard figure and 5% spoken claim give a careful viewer reason to examine the interface and claims separately. It is reasonable to treat this as a product walkthrough with unverified promotional claims, rather than evidence that the depicted controls have delivered the promised return.

citations.quote: stake BNB and earn a fixed 5% everyday

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening links the Deposit control to a solicitation, but a screen showing a control does not show it being used. Likewise, an audit-report graphic shows what the presentation puts forward, not independent verification of the report or of future returns. Those are important limits on what the pictured interface proves.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The interface is not presented as a neutral lesson or critical test. The description tells viewers to stake BNB for 5% daily ROI, and the narration tells them to join and start making money now. Showing dashboard controls supports that invitation; it does not turn the video into an operational tutorial.

citations.quote: join us and start making money right now

opening.argument: Judge, this is plainly a promotion for a named yield-farm service, with a website and chat link. Promotion alone does not establish that the service is fraudulent. The sampled dashboard shows Deposit and Harvest controls, but not a viewer transferring BNB, surrendering credentials, or being unable to withdraw. Its affiliate section likewise does not demonstrate that referral earnings were paid or that recruiting is required. The advertised 5% daily return is an aggressive claim that calls for verification; the supplied presentation does not show the underlying transaction or outcome needed to establish how the service actually operates.

citations.quote: BNBHarvest | New Yield Farm (Binance Smart Chain)
stake BNB and earn a fixed 5% everyday

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's cited links and Deposit button establish where a viewer is directed and what the interface offers, not that any deposit was taken or that a withdrawal failed. Its concern about unverifiable audit branding is fair, but lack of independent verification is not proof that the displayed service cannot function as described.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed loss is not necessary to identify the solicitation. The video asks viewers to stake BNB for a fixed 5% every day, supplies external destinations, and urges immediate participation. The Deposit control connects that promise to a way to place funds into the advertised service. The defense's missing outcomes do not neutralize the offer actually made.
